judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

C. Saravanan, J.:— Under these Writ Petitions, the Petitioner is challenging the respective impugned orders:

This is the second round of litigation. Earlier, the petitioner had challenged the Show Cause Notice issued under Section 74 of the respective GST Enactments in W.P. Nos. 9508, 9512, 9513, 9516 & 9519 of 2024. There, after recording the concessions of the learned Advocate General for the State on behalf of the Respondents, the Court directed the Respondents to pass an order in response to the Show Cause Notice impugned therein after affording the Petitioner an opportunity of hearing. The Court while passing the aforesaid order, observed as under:

“8. It was further contended on behalf of the petitioner that the contentions of the petitioner are being disregarded as is evident from the repeated reference to Westinghouse Saxby in the intimation and show cause notices in spite of the reply to the ASMT-10 notice. On prima facie examination of the relevant documents, there is some merit in this contention. Therefore, it is made clear that it is incumbent on the respondent to duly consider all contentions raised by the petitioner objectively without any pre-determination while dealing with the petitioner's reply to the show cause notices.”

2. The case of the Petitioner is that the Petitioner is engaged in manufacture of catalysts and catalytic converters and that these are classifiable under Heading 3815 and 8421 respectively, of the Customs Tariff Act, 1975, as made applicable for determination of the tax under the respective notification issued under the respective GST Enactment.

3. It is submitted by the learned Senior Counsels that the classifications adopted by the Petitioner is specific to the catalysts and catalytic converters and therefore, to impose a rival classification under chapter Heading 8708 namely “parts and accessories of the motor vehicles of headings 8701 to 8705” is misplaced. That apart, it is submitted that the reliance placed by the Respondents on the decision of the Supreme Court of India in Westinghouse Saxby Farmer Ltd. v. Commissioner of Central Excise, (2021) 5 SCC 586 : (2021) 16 GSTR-OL 176, is also incorrect. The learned Senior Counsels have drawn attention to the decision of the Supreme Court of India in Godrej Sara Lee Ltd. v. Excise and Taxation Officer-cum-assessing authority, (2023) 109 GSTR 402 : 2023 SCC OnLine SC 95, wherein in para No. 8, the Supreme Court has held that where a pure question of law arises and if investigation into facts is unnecessary, the High Court could entertain a Writ Petition in its discretion under Article 226 of the Constitution of India. Challenge to the impugned proceedings is also on the ground that the proposals in the Show Cause Notice that preceded the impugned order was to classify catalyst and catalytic converter as bumpers and parts thereof under Sub-Heading 8708-10. It is submitted that the Petitioner has been classifying products under the senior previous regime, which was in force till 30-6-2017, under the Heading 3815 and 8421 respectively. Therefore, departure in the accepted classification was unwarranted. That apart, the learned Senior Counsels also drew the attention to a recent classification accepted in the case of imports made by the Petitioner for similar item.

4. The learned counsel for the Respondent on the other hand would submit that although there was a reference to sub-headings 8708-10-90 of the Customs Tariff Act, 1975, the demand that has been confirmed on the catalyst and catalytic converter is under 8708-92-00 for - Silencers (mufflers) and exhaust pipes; parts thereof, under heading - Other parts and accessories.

5. Having considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the Petitioner and the Respondents and considering the fact that there are no other disputed question of facts warranting detailed investigation, I am inclined to admit the Writ Petition in the light of paragraph No. 8 of Godrej Sara Lee Ltd. v. Excise and Taxation Officer-cum-assessing authority. Considering the fact that the Petitioner is otherwise required to pre-deposit the amounts as per Section 107(6B), while entertaining this Writ Petition, I direct the Petitioner to deposit approximately Rs 2,41,00,00,000 (Rupees Two Hundred and Forty One Crores Only) as against the total demand confirmed vide impugned orders dated 31-12-2025, 31-12-2025, 31-12-2025, 21-1-2026 and 3-2-2026, which the Petitioner would have been liable to pre-deposit had the Petitioner approved the appellate authority, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

6. Meanwhile, Respondents shall file counter, if any, by the next date of hearing. List on 10-6-2026, for reporting compliance, for counter and for further order at 2.15 p.m.
